==English== ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*kap-|id1=head}} From {{inh|en|enm|beheden}}, {{m|enm|bihefden}}, {{m|enm|biheveden}}, from {{inh|en|ang|behēafdian|t=to behead}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*bihaubudōn}}, {{m|gmw-pro|*bihaubidōn|t=to behead}}, equivalent to {{pre|en|be|t1=off, away|head}}. Cognate with {{cog|gmh|behoubeten|t=to behead}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/bɪˈhɛd/}} ** {{IPA|en|/bəˈhɛd/|a=weak vowel merger}} * {{audio|en|En-us-behead.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛd|s=2}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb}} [[File:Beheading of Leonard George Siffleet restored.jpg|thumb|{{w|Leonard Siffleet}}, an Australian [[prisoner of war]], was beheaded by Japanese soldiers in 1943.]] # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[deliberately]] [[remove]] the [[head]] of; to [[cut off]] (someone's) [[head]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1999|author={{w|Seamus Heaney}}|title={{w|Beowulf}}|publisher=Faber and Faber|chapter=|location=London|page=68|passage=“For a while it was hand-to-hand between us,
then blood went curling along the currents
and I '''beheaded''' Grendel's mother in the hall
with a mighty sword.”]}} ====Synonyms==== * {{l|en|decapitate}} * {{l|en|decollate}} ====Derived terms==== {{col|en|beheadable|beheadal|beheaded|beheadee|beheader|beheading|beheadment}} ====Translations==== {{trans-top|to remove the head}} * Arabic: * Aramaic: * Armenian: * Aromanian: * Belarusian: * Bulgarian: * Burmese: * Catalan: * Chinese: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Estonian: * Faroese: * Finnish: * French: * Georgian: * German: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Hungarian: * Indonesian: * Italian: * Japanese: * Khmer: * Korean: * Kurdish: * Lao: * Latin: * Luxembourgish: * Macedonian: * Malay: * Māori: * Norwegian: * Old English: * Old Saxon: * Persian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Quechua: * Romagnol: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|обезгла́вливать|impf}}, {{t+|ru|обезгла́вить|pf}}, {{t|ru|[[отруба́ть]] [[голова|го́лову]]|impf}}, {{t|ru|[[отруби́ть]] [[голова|го́лову]]|pf}} * Sinhalese: * Slovak: * Slovene: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Tagalog: * Tamil: * Thai: * Turkish: * Ukrainian: * Urdu: * Uyghur: * Vietnamese: * Welsh: {{trans-bottom}} {{C|en|Death|Violence}}
